summary: A CBS Sports roundup of NASCAR offseason news for the week of Dec. 4, 2023. It covers a two-day Next Gen car test at Phoenix Raceway (splitters, diffusers, tires, mufflers), spotter and crew chief changes including at Spire Motorsports, and driver moves such as Aric Almirola's expected part-time Xfinity role with Joe Gibbs Racing, Noah Gragson's expected move to Stewart-Haas Racing and uncertainty over Kaulig Racing's No. 16.
one_line: Roundup of NASCAR's early-December 2023 offseason: Phoenix Next Gen testing, spotter and crew chief changes, and driver moves for 2024.
key_facts: Ryan Blaney, Chris Buescher, Erik Jones, Christopher Bell, Kyle Larson and Corey LaJoie took part in a two-day Next Gen car test at Phoenix Raceway, one month after Blaney was crowned Cup Series champion.
Day one of the Phoenix test focused on different splitters and diffusers and on tires engineered to degrade more during green flag runs, to build on marginal 2023 short track package improvements.
Teams ran a simplified diffuser with just two fins in the middle at a 90-degree angle, plus an alternate splitter design, per Cole Cusumano.
Day two tested existing mufflers to soften Cup Series engine noise; gearbox and shifting changes were not part of the test.
Blaney said the alternate splitter, which significantly reduced downforce, was the biggest change: "It's a massive aero loss when you do that."
Kyle Larson said he noticed no difference in cockpit cooling with the mufflers and said the cars are "way too loud, and probably are still too loud with the mufflers."
Chase Elliott's spotter Eddie D'Hondt and Ryan Blaney's spotter Josh Williams both announced they are stepping down for 2024.
Tim Fedewa, longtime spotter for Kevin Harvick, is expected to take over as Blaney's spotter, per Bob Pockrass of Fox Sports.

Spire Motorsports hired Stephen Doran (from Stewart-Haas Racing) as crew chief for Zane Smith's No. 71 Chevrolet and Luke Lambert (from Legacy Motor Club's No. 42) as crew chief of Carson Hocevar's No. 77.
Spire Motorsports also hired Doug Duchardt, formerly of General Motors and Chip Ganassi Racing, as team president.

Joe Gibbs appeared to tell Commanders owner Josh Harris that Aric Almirola is now driving for them; Almirola is expected to run part-time in the Xfinity Series for Joe Gibbs Racing alongside Chandler Smith and Sheldon Creed.
Noah Gragson is widely expected to take over Stewart-Haas Racing's No. 10 after resigning from Legacy Motor Club's No. 42 in August during a suspension for liking a racially insensitive meme.
A.J. Allmendinger will return to full-time Xfinity Series racing for Kaulig Racing in 2024 while continuing a partial Cup schedule, leaving the No. 16 driver uncertain.
Matt Weaver said reports that Ty Dillon had been hired for Kaulig's No. 16 were "incorrect."
